<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="74.42px"/><col width="539.75px"/><tr height="136.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 31</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">JQDIS</span>: Injected Queue disable</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are set and cleared by software to disable the Injected Queue mechanism :</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Injected Queue enabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Injected Queue disabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write this bit only when ADSTART = 0 and JADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no regular nor injected conversion is ongoing).</p><p class="RegTNote_">A set or reset of JQDIS bit causes the injected queue to be flushed and the ADC_JSQR register is cleared.</p></td></tr><tr height="216.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 30:26</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">AWD1CH[4:0]</span>: Analog watchdog 1 channel selection</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are set and cleared by software. They select the input channel to be guarded by the analog watchdog.</p><p class="TableIndent">00000: ADC analog input channel 0 monitored by AWD1</p><p class="TableIndent">00001: ADC analog input channel 1 monitored by AWD1</p><p class="TableIndent">.....</p><p class="TableIndent">10010: ADC analog input channel 18 monitored by AWD1</p><p class="TableIndent">others: reserved, must not be used</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>Some channels are not connected physically. Keep the corresponding <span class="BOLD">AWD1CH[4:0] setting to </span>the reset value.</p><p class="RegTNote_">The channel selected by AWD1CH must be also selected into the SQi or JSQi bits.</p><p class="RegTNote_">The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 and JADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr height="164.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 25</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">JAUTO:</span> Automatic injected group conversion</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to enable/disable automatic injected group conversion after regular group conversion.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Automatic injected group conversion disabled<br/>1: Automatic injected group conversion enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write this bit only when ADSTART = 0 and JADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no regular nor injected conversion is ongoing).</p><p class="RegTNote_"><span data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_">When dual mode is enabled (DUAL bits in ADCx_CCR register are not equal to zero), the bit JAUTO of the slave ADC is no more writable and its content is equal to the bit JAUTO of the </span><span data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_">master ADC.</span></p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">JAWD1EN</span>: Analog watchdog 1 enable on injected channels</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Analog watchdog 1 disabled on injected channels</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Analog watchdog 1 enabled on injected channels</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write this bit only when JADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no injected conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 23</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">AWD1EN</span>: Analog watchdog 1 enable on regular channels</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Analog watchdog 1 disabled on regular channels</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Analog watchdog 1 enabled on regular channels</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write this bit only when ADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no regular conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr height="118.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 22</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">AWD1SGL</span>: Enable the watchdog 1 on a single channel or on all channels</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to enable the analog watchdog on the channel identified by the AWD1CH[4:0] bits or on all the channels</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Analog watchdog 1 enabled on all channels</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Analog watchdog 1 enabled on a single channel</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 and JADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr height="226.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 21</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">JQM</span>: ADC_JSQR queue mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">It defines how an empty Queue is managed.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: ADC_JSQR mode 0: The Queue is never empty and maintains the last written configuration into ADC_JSQR.</p><p class="TableIndent">1: ADC_JSQR mode 1: The Queue can be empty and when this occurs, the software and hardware triggers of the injected sequence are both internally disabled just after the completion of the last valid injected sequence.</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to <a href="#XREF_40313__1_4_15_Queue_of_Context_for_Injected_Conversions10" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 21.4.21: Queue of context for injected conversions</a> for more information.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write this bit only when JADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no injected conversion is ongoing).</p><p class="RegTNote_"><span data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_">When dual mode is enabled (DUAL bits in ADCx_CCR register are not equal to zero), the bit JQM of the slave ADC is no more writable and its content is equal to the bit JQM of the master </span><span data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_">ADC.</span></p></td></tr><tr height="196.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">JDISCEN</span><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">:</span> Discontinuous mode on injected channels</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to enable/disable discontinuous mode on the injected channels of a group.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Discontinuous mode on injected channels disabled<br/>1: Discontinuous mode on injected channels enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write this bit only when JADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no injected conversion is ongoing).</p><p class="RegTNote_">It is not possible to use both auto-injected mode and discontinuous mode simultaneously: the bits DISCEN and JDISCEN must be kept cleared by software when JAUTO is set.</p><p class="RegTNote_"><span data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_">When dual mode is enabled (bits DUAL of ADCx_CCR register are not equal to zero), the bit JDISCEN of the slave ADC is no more writable and its content is equal to the bit JDISCEN of </span><span data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_">the master ADC.</span></p></td></tr><tr height="193.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 19:17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DISCNUM[2:0]</span><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">:</span> Discontinuous mode channel count</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are written by software to define the number of regular channels to be converted in discontinuous mode, after receiving an external trigger.</p><p class="TableIndent">000: 1 channel<br/>001: 2 channels<br/>...<br/>111: 8 channels</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no regular conversion is ongoing).</p><p class="RegTNote_"><span data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_">When dual mode is enabled (DUAL bits in ADCx_CCR register are not equal to zero), the bits DISCNUM[2:0] of the slave ADC are no more writable and their content is equal to the bits </span><span data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_">DISCNUM[2:0] of the master ADC.</span></p></td></tr><tr height="214.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DISCEN</span>: Discontinuous mode for regular channels</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to enable/disable Discontinuous mode for regular channels.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Discontinuous mode for regular channels disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Discontinuous mode for regular channels enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>It is not possible to have both discontinuous mode and continuous mode enabled: it is forbidden to set both DISCEN = 1 and CONT = 1.</p><p class="RegTNote_">It is not possible to use both auto-injected mode and discontinuous mode simultaneously: the bits DISCEN and JDISCEN must be kept cleared by software when JAUTO is set. </p><p class="RegTNote_">The software is allowed to write this bit only when ADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no regular conversion is ongoing).</p><p class="RegTNote_"><span data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_">When dual mode is enabled (DUAL bits in ADCx_CCR register are not equal to zero), the bit DISCEN of the slave ADC is no more writable and its content is equal to the bit DISCEN of the </span><span data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_">master ADC.</span></p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_adc_16trigevents,_adc_vref_" height="22.67px" style="display: none"><td data-conditional="_adc_16trigevents,_adc_vref_" style="display: none"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 15</p></td><td data-conditional="_adc_16trigevents,_adc_vref_" style="display: none"><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_adc_32trigevents,_adc_vref_" height="118.67px"><td data-conditional="_adc_32trigevents,_adc_vref_"><p class="RegTBodyR" style="color:#ff0000;"><span style="color:#000000;">Bit 15</span></p></td><td data-conditional="_adc_32trigevents,_adc_vref_"><p class="TableBodyL" style="color:#ff0000;"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;color:#000000;">ALIGN</span><span style="color:#000000;">: Data alignment</span></p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to select right or left alignment. Refer to <a href="#XREF_15986__1_6_1_Data_Register_&amp;_Data_Alignment_(ADC_DR%2C_ADC_DRx%2C_ADC_JOFFx%2C10" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Data register, data alignment and offset (ADC_DR, OFFSETy, OFFSETy_CH, ALIGN)</a>.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Right alignment</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Left alignment</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write this bit only when ADSTART = 0 and JADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr height="150.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 14</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">AUTDLY</span>: Delayed conversion mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to enable/disable the Auto Delayed Conversion mode.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Auto-delayed conversion mode off</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Auto-delayed conversion mode on</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write this bit only when ADSTART = 0 and JADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p><p class="RegTNote_"><span data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_">When dual mode is enabled (DUAL bits in ADCx_CCR register are not equal to zero), the bit AUTDLY of the slave ADC is no more writable and its content is equal to the bit AUTDLY of the </span><span data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_">master ADC.</span></p></td></tr><tr height="197.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 13</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">CONT</span>: Single / continuous conversion mode for regular conversions</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software. If it is set, regular conversion takes place continuously until it is cleared.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Single conversion mode</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Continuous conversion mode</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>It is not possible to have both discontinuous mode and continuous mode enabled: it is forbidden to set both DISCEN = 1 and CONT = 1.</p><p class="RegTNote_">The software is allowed to write this bit only when ADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no regular conversion is ongoing).</p><p class="RegTNote_"><span data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_">When dual mode is enabled (DUAL bits in ADCx_CCR register are not equal to zero), the bit CONT of the slave ADC is no more writable and its content is equal to the bit CONT of the </span><span data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_">master ADC.</span></p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">OVRMOD</span>: Overrun mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software and configure the way data overrun is managed.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: ADC_DR register is preserved with the old data when an overrun is detected. </p><p class="TableIndent">1: ADC_DR register is overwritten with the last conversion result when an overrun is detected.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write this bit only when ADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no regular conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr height="146.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 11:10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">EXTEN[1:0]</span>: External trigger enable and polarity selection for regular channels</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are set and cleared by software to select the external trigger polarity and enable the trigger of a regular group.</p><p class="TableIndent">00: Hardware trigger detection disabled (conversions can be launched by software)<br/>01: Hardware trigger detection on the rising edge<br/>10: Hardware trigger detection on the falling edge<br/>11: Hardware trigger detection on both the rising and falling edges</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no regular conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_adc_16trigevents,_adc_vref_" height="229.33px" style="display: none"><td data-conditional="_adc_16trigevents,_adc_vref_" style="display: none"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 9:6</p></td><td data-conditional="_adc_16trigevents,_adc_vref_" style="display: none"><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">EXTSEL[3:0]</span>: External trigger selection for regular group</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits select the external event used to trigger the start of conversion of a regular group:</p><p class="TableIndent">0000: Event 0</p><p class="TableIndent">0001: Event 1</p><p class="TableIndent">0010: Event 2</p><p class="TableIndent">0011: Event 3</p><p class="TableIndent">0100: Event 4</p><p class="TableIndent">0101: Event 5</p><p class="TableIndent">0110: Event 6</p><p class="TableIndent">0111: Event 7<br/>...<br/>1111: Event 15</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no regular conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_adc_32trigevents,_adc_vref_" height="229.33px"><td data-conditional="_adc_32trigevents,_adc_vref_"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 9:5</p></td><td data-conditional="_adc_32trigevents,_adc_vref_"><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">EXTSEL[4:0]</span>: External trigger selection for regular group</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits select the external event used to trigger the start of conversion of a regular group:</p><p class="TableIndent">00000: Event 0</p><p class="TableIndent">00001: Event 1</p><p class="TableIndent">00010: Event 2</p><p class="TableIndent">00011: Event 3</p><p class="TableIndent">00100: Event 4</p><p class="TableIndent">00101: Event 5</p><p class="TableIndent">00110: Event 6</p><p class="TableIndent">00111: Event 7<br/>...<br/>11111: Event 31</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no regular conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_adc_16trigevents,_adc_vref_" height="118.67px" style="display: none"><td data-conditional="_adc_16trigevents,_adc_vref_" style="display: none"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td data-conditional="_adc_16trigevents,_adc_vref_" style="display: none"><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">ALIGN</span>: Data alignment</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to select right or left alignment. Refer to <a href="#XREF_15986__1_6_1_Data_Register_&amp;_Data_Alignment_(ADC_DR%2C_ADC_DRx%2C_ADC_JOFFx%2C10" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section : Data register, data alignment and offset (ADC_DR, OFFSETy, OFFSETy_CH, ALIGN)</a></p><p class="TableIndent">0: Right alignment</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Left alignment</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write this bit only when ADSTART = 0 and JADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr height="136.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 4:3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">RES[1:0]</span>: Data resolution</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are written by software to select the resolution of the conversion.</p><p class="TableIndent">00: 12-bit</p><p class="TableIndent">01: 10-bit</p><p class="TableIndent">10: 8-bit</p><p class="TableIndent">11: 6-bit</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 and JADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_adc_vref_,_noadc_dfsdm" height="22.67px"><td data-conditional="_adc_vref_,_noadc_dfsdm"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td data-conditional="_adc_vref_,_noadc_dfsdm"><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_adc_dfsdm,_adc_vref_" height="120.00px" style="display: none"><td data-conditional="_adc_dfsdm,_adc_vref_" style="display: none"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td data-conditional="_adc_dfsdm,_adc_vref_" style="display: none"><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DFSDMCFG</span>: DFSDM mode configuration</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to enable the DFSDM mode. It is effective only when</p><p class="TableIndent">DMAEN = 0.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: DFSDM mode disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: DFSDM mode enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>To make sure no conversion is ongoing, the software is allowed to write this bit only when ADSTART= 0 and JADSTART= 0.</p></td></tr><tr height="166.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DMACFG</span>: Direct memory access configuration</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to select between two DMA modes of operation. It is effective only when DMAEN<span style="font-style:Italic;"> = 1</span><span data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_" style="font-style:Italic;"> (single ADC mode), or MDMA[1:0]</span><span data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_"> ≠ 00 (dual ADC mode)</span>.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: DMA One Shot mode selected</p><p class="TableIndent">1: DMA Circular mode selected</p><p class="TableIndent">For more details, refer to <a href="#XREF_53109__1_6_5_Using_the_DMA10" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section : Managing conversions using the DMA</a></p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write this bit only when ADSTART = 0 and JADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p><p class="RegTNote_"><span data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_">In dual-ADC modes, this bit is not relevant and replaced by control bit DMACFG of the ADCx_CCR register.</span></p></td></tr><tr height="165.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DMAEN</span>: Direct memory access enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to enable the generation of DMA requests. This allows to use the DMA to manage automatically the converted data. For more details, refer to <a href="#XREF_53109__1_6_5_Using_the_DMA10" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section : Managing conversions using the DMA</a>.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: DMA disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: DMA enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write this bit only when ADSTART = 0 and JADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p><p class="RegTNote_"><span data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_">In dual-ADC modes, this bit is not relevant and replaced by control bits MDMA[1:0] of the ADCx_CCR register.</span></p></td></tr></table></div>


### 21.7.5 ADC configuration register 2 (ADC\_CFGR2)

Address offset: 0x10

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="74.42px"/><col width="539.75px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:<span data-conditional="_adc_vref_,_noadc_lftrig">28</span></p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_adc_lftrig,_adc_vref_" height="104.00px" style="display: none"><td data-conditional="_adc_lftrig,_adc_vref_" style="display: none"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 29</p></td><td data-conditional="_adc_lftrig,_adc_vref_" style="display: none"><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">LFTRIG</span>: Low-frequency trigger</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Low-frequency trigger mode disabled </p><p class="TableIndent">1: Low-frequency trigger mode enabled </p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write this bit only when ADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_adc_lftrig,_adc_vref_" height="22.67px" style="display: none"><td data-conditional="_adc_lftrig,_adc_vref_" style="display: none"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 28</p></td><td data-conditional="_adc_lftrig,_adc_vref_" style="display: none"><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_adc_flexsmp,_adc_vref_" height="166.67px"><td data-conditional="_adc_flexsmp,_adc_vref_"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 27</p></td><td data-conditional="_adc_flexsmp,_adc_vref_"><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">SMPTRIG</span>: Sampling time control trigger mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to enable the sampling time control trigger mode.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Sampling time control trigger mode disabled </p><p class="TableIndent">1: Sampling time control trigger mode enabled</p><p class="TableIndent">The sampling time starts on the trigger rising edge, and the conversion on the trigger falling edge.</p><p class="TableIndent">EXTEN[1:0] bits should be set to 01. BULB bit must not be set when the SMPTRIG bit is set.</p><p class="TableIndent">When EXTEN[1:0] bits are set to 00, set SWTRIG to start the sampling and clear SWTRIG bit to start the conversion.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write this bit only when ADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_adc_flexsmp,_adc_vref_" height="150.67px"><td data-conditional="_adc_flexsmp,_adc_vref_"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 26</p></td><td data-conditional="_adc_flexsmp,_adc_vref_"><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">BULB</span>: Bulb sampling mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to enable the bulb sampling mode.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Bulb sampling mode disabled </p><p class="TableIndent">1: Bulb sampling mode enabled. The sampling period starts just after the previous end of conversion.</p><p class="TableIndent">SAMPTRIG bit must not be set when the BULB bit is set. </p><p class="TableIndent">The very first ADC conversion is performed with the sampling time specified in SMPx bits.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write this bit only when ADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_adc_flexsmp,_adc_vref_" height="104.00px"><td data-conditional="_adc_flexsmp,_adc_vref_"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 25</p></td><td data-conditional="_adc_flexsmp,_adc_vref_"><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">SWTRIG</span>: Software trigger bit for sampling time control trigger mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to enable the bulb sampling mode.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Software trigger starts the conversion for sampling time control trigger mode </p><p class="TableIndent">1: Software trigger starts the sampling for sampling time control trigger mode </p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write this bit only when ADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits <span data-conditional="_adc_flexsmp,_adc_vref_">24</span>:17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_adc_gainoffset_comp,_adc_vref_" height="104.00px"><td data-conditional="_adc_gainoffset_comp,_adc_vref_"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 16</p></td><td data-conditional="_adc_gainoffset_comp,_adc_vref_"><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">GCOMP</span>: Gain compensation mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to enable the gain compensation mode.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Regular ADC operating mode </p><p class="TableIndent">1: Gain compensation enabled and applied on all channels</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write this bit only when ADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits <span data-conditional="_adc_gainoffset_comp,_adc_vref_">15</span>:11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="162.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">ROVSM</span>: Regular Oversampling mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to select the regular oversampling mode.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Continued mode: When injected conversions are triggered, the oversampling is temporary stopped and continued after the injection sequence (oversampling buffer is maintained during injected sequence)</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Resumed mode: When injected conversions are triggered, the current oversampling is aborted and resumed from start after the injection sequence (oversampling buffer is zeroed by injected sequence start)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write this bit only when ADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 9</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">TROVS</span>: Triggered Regular Oversampling</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to enable triggered oversampling</p><p class="TableIndent">0: All oversampled conversions for a channel are done consecutively following a trigger</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Each oversampled conversion for a channel needs a new trigger</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write this bit only when ADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr height="246.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 8:5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">OVSS[3:0]</span><span class="BOLD">: Oversampling shift</span></p><p class="TableIndent"><span class="BOLD">This bitfield is set and cleared by software to define the right shifting applied to the raw oversampling result.</span></p><p class="TableIndent"><span class="BOLD">0000: No shift</span></p><p class="TableIndent"><span class="BOLD">0001: Shift 1-bit</span></p><p class="TableIndent"><span class="BOLD">0010: Shift 2-bits</span></p><p class="TableIndent"><span class="BOLD">0011: Shift 3-bits</span></p><p class="TableIndent"><span class="BOLD">0100: Shift 4-bits</span></p><p class="TableIndent"><span class="BOLD">0101: Shift 5-bits</span></p><p class="TableIndent"><span class="BOLD">0110: Shift 6-bits</span></p><p class="TableIndent"><span class="BOLD">0111: Shift 7-bits</span></p><p class="TableIndent"><span class="BOLD">1000: Shift 8-bits</span></p><p class="TableIndent"><span class="BOLD">Other codes reserved</span></p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr height="200.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 4:2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">OVSR[2:0]</span><span class="BOLD">: Oversampling ratio</span></p><p class="TableIndent"><span class="BOLD">This bitfield is set and cleared by software to define the oversampling ratio.</span></p><p class="TableIndent"><span class="BOLD">000: 2x</span></p><p class="TableIndent"><span class="BOLD">001: 4x</span></p><p class="TableIndent"><span class="BOLD">010: 8x</span></p><p class="TableIndent"><span class="BOLD">011: 16x</span></p><p class="TableIndent"><span class="BOLD">100: 32x</span></p><p class="TableIndent"><span class="BOLD">101: 64x</span></p><p class="TableIndent"><span class="BOLD">110: 128x</span></p><p class="TableIndent"><span class="BOLD">111: 256x</span></p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">JOVSE</span>: Injected Oversampling Enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to enable injected oversampling.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Injected Oversampling disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Injected Oversampling enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write this bit only when ADSTART = 0 and JADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing)</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">ROVSE</span>: Regular Oversampling Enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to enable regular oversampling.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Regular Oversampling disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Regular Oversampling enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write this bit only when ADSTART = 0 and JADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing)</p></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.40px"/><col width="497.23px"/><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 31</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span data-conditional="_adc_smpplus,_adc_vref_" style="font-weight:Bold;">SMPPLUS: </span><span data-conditional="_adc_smpplus,_adc_vref_">Addition of one clock cycle to the sampling time</span></p><p class="TableIndent"><span data-conditional="_adc_smpplus,_adc_vref_">1: 2.5 ADC clock cycle sampling time becomes 3.5 ADC clock cycles for the ADC_SMPR1 and ADC_SMPR2 registers.</span></p><p class="TableIndent"><span data-conditional="_adc_smpplus,_adc_vref_">0: The sampling time remains set to 2.5 ADC clock cycles remains </span></p><p class="TableBodyL" style="font-style:Italic;"><span data-conditional="_adc_smpplus,_adc_vref_">To make sure no conversion is ongoing, the software is allowed to write this bit only when ADSTART= 0 and JADSTART= 0.</span></p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_adc_smpplus,_adc_vref_" height="22.67px"><td data-conditional="_adc_smpplus,_adc_vref_"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 30</p></td><td data-conditional="_adc_smpplus,_adc_vref_"><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="246.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 29:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SMPx[2:0]:</span><span style="font-weight:Bold;font-style:Italic;"> </span>Channel x sampling time selection (x = 9 to 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are written by software to select the sampling time individually for each channel. During sample cycles, the channel selection bits must remain unchanged.</p><p class="TableIndent">000: 2.5 ADC clock cycles</p><p class="TableIndent">001: 6.5 ADC clock cycles</p><p class="TableIndent">010: 12.5 ADC clock cycles</p><p class="TableIndent">011: 24.5 ADC clock cycles</p><p class="TableIndent">100: 47.5 ADC clock cycles</p><p class="TableIndent">101: 92.5 ADC clock cycles</p><p class="TableIndent">110: 247.5 ADC clock cycles</p><p class="TableIndent">111: 640.5 ADC clock cycles</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 and JADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p><p class="RegTNote_">Some channels are not connected physically. Keep the corresponding <span class="BOLD">SMPx[2:0] setting to </span>the reset value.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 21.7.7 ADC sample time register 2 (ADC\_SMPR2)

Address offset: 0x18

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

During sampling cycles, the channel selection bits must remain unchanged.</p><p class="TableIndent">000: 2.5 ADC clock cycles</p><p class="TableIndent">001: 6.5 ADC clock cycles</p><p class="TableIndent">010: 12.5 ADC clock cycles</p><p class="TableIndent">011: 24.5 ADC clock cycles</p><p class="TableIndent">100: 47.5 ADC clock cycles</p><p class="TableIndent">101: 92.5 ADC clock cycles</p><p class="TableIndent">110: 247.5 ADC clock cycles</p><p class="TableIndent">111: 640.5 ADC clock cycles</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 and JADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p><p class="RegTNote_">Some channels are not connected physically. Keep the corresponding <span class="BOLD">SMPx[2:0] setting to </span>the reset value.</p></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="74.42px"/><col width="539.75px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:28</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 27:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">HT1[11:0]</span>: Analog watchdog 1 higher threshold</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are written by software to define the higher threshold for the analog watchdog 1. </p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to <a href="#XREF_35523__1_7_Analog_window_watchdog_(AWDxEN%2C_JAWDxEN%2C_AWDxSGL%2C10" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 21.4.28: Analog window watchdog (AWD1EN, JAWD1EN, AWD1SGL, AWD1CH, AWD2CH, AWD3CH, AWD_HTx, AWD_LTx, AWDx)</a>.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 and JADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 15</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_adc_awdgflt,_adc_vref_" height="136.00px"><td data-conditional="_adc_awdgflt,_adc_vref_"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 14:12</p></td><td data-conditional="_adc_awdgflt,_adc_vref_"><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">AWDFILT</span>: Analog watchdog filtering parameter</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">000: No filtering </p><p class="TableIndent">001: two consecutive detection generates an AWDx flag or an interrupt</p><p class="TableIndent">...</p><p class="TableIndent">111: Eight consecutive detection generates an AWDx flag or an interrupt</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write this bit only when ADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 11:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">LT1[11:0]</span>: Analog watchdog 1 lower threshold</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are written by software to define the lower threshold for the analog watchdog 1.</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to <a href="#XREF_35523__1_7_Analog_window_watchdog_(AWDxEN%2C_JAWDxEN%2C_AWDxSGL%2C10" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 21.4.28: Analog window watchdog (AWD1EN, JAWD1EN, AWD1SGL, AWD1CH, AWD2CH, AWD3CH, AWD_HTx, AWD_LTx, AWDx)</a></p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 and JADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 21.7.9 ADC watchdog threshold register 2 (ADC\_TR2)

Address offset: 0x24

Reset value: 0x00FF 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="74.42px"/><col width="539.75px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 23:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">HT3[7:0]</span>: Analog watchdog 3 higher threshold</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are written by software to define the higher threshold for the analog watchdog 3.</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to <a href="#XREF_35523__1_7_Analog_window_watchdog_(AWDxEN%2C_JAWDxEN%2C_AWDxSGL%2C10" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 21.4.28: Analog window watchdog (AWD1EN, JAWD1EN, AWD1SGL, AWD1CH, AWD2CH, AWD3CH, AWD_HTx, AWD_LTx, AWDx)</a></p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 and JADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="88.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">LT3[7:0]</span>: Analog watchdog 3 lower threshold</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are written by software to define the lower threshold for the analog watchdog 3.</p><p class="TableIndent">This watchdog compares the 8-bit of LT3 with the 8 MSB of the converted data.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 and JADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr></table></div>

font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">:</span> fourth conversion in regular sequence</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are written by software with the channel number (0 to 18) assigned as the fourth in the regular conversion sequence.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no regular conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 23</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 22:18</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SQ3[4:0]</span><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">:</span> second conversion in regular sequence</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are written by software with the channel number (0 to 18) assigned as the second in the regular conversion sequence.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no regular conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 10:6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SQ1[4:0]</span><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">:</span> first conversion in regular sequence</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are written by software with the channel number (0 to 18) assigned as the first in the regular conversion sequence.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no regular conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 5:4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="146.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 3:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">L[3:0]</span><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">:</span> Regular channel sequence length</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are written by software to define the total number of conversions in the regular channel conversion sequence.</p><p class="TableIndent">0000: 1 conversion<br/>0001: 2 conversions<br/>...<br/>1111: 16 conversions</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no regular conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr></table></div>


**Note:**

Some channels are not connected physically and must not be selected for conversion.

### 21.7.12 ADC regular sequence register 2 (ADC\_SQR2)

Address offset: 0x34

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

### 21.7.13 ADC regular sequence register 3 (ADC\_SQR3)

Address offset: 0x38

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

### 21.7.14 ADC regular sequence register 4 (ADC\_SQR4)

Address offset: 0x3C

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="114.73px"/><col width="497.23px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 10:6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SQ16[4:0]</span><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">:</span> 16th conversion in regular sequence</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are written by software with the channel number (0 to 18) assigned as the 16th in the regular conversion sequence.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no regular conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 4:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SQ15[4:0]</span><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">:</span> 15th conversion in regular sequence</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are written by software with the channel number (0 to 18) assigned as the 15th in the regular conversion sequence.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no regular conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr></table></div>


**Note:**

Some channels are not connected physically and must not be selected for conversion.

### 21.7.15 ADC regular data register (ADC\_DR)

Address offset: 0x40

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

data-conditional="_adc_16trigevents,_adc_vref_" style="display: none"><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">JEXTEN[1:0]</span>: External Trigger Enable and Polarity Selection for injected channels</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are set and cleared by software to select the external trigger polarity and enable the trigger of an injected group. </p><p class="TableIndent">00: If JQDIS = 0 (queue enabled), Hardware and software trigger detection disabled<br/>00: If JQDIS = 1 (queue disabled), Hardware trigger detection disabled (conversions can be launched by software)<br/>01: Hardware trigger detection on the rising edge<br/>10: Hardware trigger detection on the falling edge<br/>11: Hardware trigger detection on both the rising and falling edges</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when JADSTART = 0 (which ensures that <span style="font-kerning:none;">no injected conversion is ongoing).</span></p><p class="RegTNote_">If JQM = 1 and if the Queue of Context becomes empty, the software and hardware triggers of the injected sequence are both internally disabled (refer to <a href="#XREF_40313__1_4_15_Queue_of_Context_for_Injected_Conversions10" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 21.4.21: Queue of context for injected conversions</a>)</p></td></tr><tr **Note:**

Some channels are not connected physically and must not be selected for conversion.

### 21.7.17 ADC offset y register (ADC\_OFRy)

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="114.73px"/><col width="498.56px"/><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 31</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OFFSET_EN</span><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">:</span> Offset y enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is written by software to enable or disable the offset programmed into bits OFFSETy[11:0]. </p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write this bit only when ADSTART = 0 and JADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr height="118.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 30:26</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OFFSET_CH[4:0]</span><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">:</span> Channel selection for the data offset y</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are written by software to define the channel to which the offset programmed into bits OFFSETy[11:0] applies. </p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 and JADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p><p class="RegTNote_">Some channels are not connected physically and must not be selected for the data offset y. </p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_adc_gainoffset_comp,_adc_vref_" height="118.67px"><td data-conditional="_adc_gainoffset_comp,_adc_vref_"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 25</p></td><td data-conditional="_adc_gainoffset_comp,_adc_vref_"><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">SATEN</span>: Saturation enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to enable the saturation at 0x000 and 0xFFF for the offset function.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No saturation control, offset result can be signed</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Saturation enabled, offset result unsigned and saturated at 0x000 and 0xFFF</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 and JADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_adc_gainoffset_comp,_adc_vref_" height="104.00px"><td data-conditional="_adc_gainoffset_comp,_adc_vref_"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 24</p></td><td data-conditional="_adc_gainoffset_comp,_adc_vref_"><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">OFFSETPOS</span>: Positive offset </p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to enable the positive offset.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Negative offset </p><p class="TableIndent">1: Positive offset </p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 and JADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits <span data-conditional="_adc_gainoffset_comp,_adc_vref_">23</span>:12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="192.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 11:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OFFSET[11:0]</span><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">:</span> Data offset y for the channel programmed into bits OFFSETy_CH[4:0]</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are written by software to define the offset y to be subtracted from the raw converted data when converting a channel (can be regular or injected). The channel to which applies the data offset y must be programmed in the bits OFFSETy_CH[4:0]. The conversion result can be read from in the ADC_DR (regular conversion) or from in the ADC_JDRyi registers (injected conversion). </p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 and JADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p><p class="RegTNote_">If several offset (OFFSETy) point to the same channel, only the offset with the lowest x value is considered for the subtraction. <br/>Ex: if OFFSET1_CH[4:0]=4 and OFFSET2_CH[4:0]=4, this is OFFSET1[11:0] which is subtracted when converting channel 4.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 21.7.18 ADC injected channel y data register (ADC\_JDRy)

Address offset: 0x80 + 0x04 \* (y - 1), (y = 1 to 4)

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="74.42px"/><col width="539.75px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:19</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="184.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 18:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">AWD2CH[18:0]</span>: Analog watchdog 2 channel selection</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are set and cleared by software. They enable and select the input channels to be guarded by the analog watchdog 2.</p><p class="TableIndent">AWD2CH[i] = 0: ADC analog input channel i is not monitored by AWD2</p><p class="TableIndent">AWD2CH[i] = 1: ADC analog input channel i is monitored by AWD2</p><p class="TableIndent">When AWD2CH[18:0] = 000..0, the analog watchdog 2 is disabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The channels selected by AWD2CH must be also selected into the SQi or JSQi bits.</p><p class="RegTNote_">The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 and JADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p><p class="RegTNote_">Some channels are not connected physically and must not be selected for the analog watchdog. </p></td></tr></table></div>


### 21.7.20 ADC analog watchdog 3 configuration register (ADC\_AWD3CR)

Address offset: 0xA4

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="74.42px"/><col width="539.75px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:19</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="185.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 18:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">AWD3CH[18:0]</span>: Analog watchdog 3 channel selection</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are set and cleared by software. They enable and select the input channels to be guarded by the analog watchdog 3.</p><p class="TableIndent">AWD3CH[i] = 0: ADC analog input channel i is not monitored by AWD3</p><p class="TableIndent">AWD3CH[i] = 1: ADC analog input channel i is monitored by AWD3</p><p class="TableBodyL">When AWD3CH[18:0] = 000..0, the analog watchdog 3 is disabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The channels selected by AWD3CH must be also selected into the SQi or JSQi bits.</p><p class="RegTNote_">The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 and JADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no conversion is ongoing).</p><p class="RegTNote_">Some channels are not connected physically and must not be selected for the analog watchdog. </p></td></tr></table></div>


### 21.7.21 ADC differential mode selection register (ADC\_DIFSEL)

Address offset: 0xB0

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="74.42px"/><col width="539.75px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:19</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="150.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 18:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">DIFSEL[</span><span style="font-weight:Bold;">18</span><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">:0]</span>: Differential mode for channels 18 to 0.</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are set and cleared by software. They allow to select if a channel is configured as single-ended or differential mode.</p><p class="TableIndent">DIFSEL[i] = 0: ADC analog input channel is configured in single ended mode</p><p class="TableIndent">DIFSEL[i] = 1: ADC analog input channel i is configured in differential mode</p><p class="RegTNote" style="font-style:normal;">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The DIFSEL bits corresponding to channels that are either connected to a single-ended I/O port or to an internal channel must be kept their reset value (single-ended input mode).</p><p class="RegTNote_">The software is allowed to write these bits only when the ADC is disabled (ADCAL = 0, JADSTART = 0, JADSTP = 0, ADSTART = 0, ADSTP = 0, ADDIS = 0 and ADEN = 0).</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 21.7.22 ADC calibration factors (ADC\_CALFACT)

Address offset: 0xB4

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="74.42px"/><col width="539.75px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:23</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="148.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 22:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">CALFACT_D[6:0]</span>: Calibration Factors in differential mode</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are written by hardware or by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">Once a differential inputs calibration is complete, they are updated by hardware with the calibration factors.</p><p class="TableIndent">Software can write these bits with a new calibration factor. If the new calibration factor is different from the current one stored into the analog ADC, it is then applied once a new differential calibration is launched.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADEN = 1, ADSTART = 0 and JADSTART = 0 (ADC is enabled and no calibration is ongoing and no conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="148.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 6:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">CALFACT_S[6:0]</span>: Calibration Factors In single-ended mode</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are written by hardware or by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">Once a single-ended inputs calibration is complete, they are updated by hardware with the calibration factors.</p><p class="TableIndent">Software can write these bits with a new calibration factor. If the new calibration factor is different from the current one stored into the analog ADC, it is then applied once a new single-ended calibration is launched.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADEN = 1, ADSTART = 0 and JADSTART = 0 (ADC is enabled and no calibration is ongoing and no conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left" data-conditional="_adc_gainoffset_comp,_adc_vref_"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="74.42px"/><col width="539.75px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:14</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="169.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 13:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="BOLD" style="font-weight:Bold;">GCOMPCOEFF[13:0]</span>: Gain compensation coefficient</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are set and cleared by software to program the gain compensation coefficient.</p><p class="TableIndent">00 1000 0000 0000: gain factor of 0.5</p><p class="TableIndent">...</p><p class="TableIndent">01 0000 0000 0000: gain factor of 1</p><p class="TableIndent">10 0000 0000 0000: gain factor of 2</p><p class="TableIndent">11 0000 0000 0000: gain factor of 3</p><p class="TableIndent">...</p><p class="TableIndent">The coefficient is divided by 4096 to get the gain factor ranging from 0 to 3.999756.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This gain compensation is only applied when GCOMP bit of ADC_CFGR2 register is 1.</p></td></tr></table></div>


## 21.8 ADC common registers

These registers define the control and status registers common to master and slave ADCs:

### 21.8.1 ADCx common status register (ADCx\_CSR) (x = 12 or 345)

Address offset: 0x300

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

This register provides an image of the status bits of the different ADCs. Nevertheless it is read-only and does not allow to clear the different status bits. Instead each status bit must be cleared by writing 0 to it in the corresponding ADC\_ISR register.

One interface controls ADC1 and ADC2, while the other interface controls ADC3, ADC4 and ADC5.

### 21.8.2 ADCx common control register (ADCx\_CCR) (x = 12 or 345)

Address offset: 0x308

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

One interface controls ADC1 and ADC2, while the other interface controls ADC3, ADC4 and ADC5.

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="114.73px"/><col width="497.89px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:25</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="70.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span data-conditional="_adc_vref_,RM0440" style="font-weight:Bold;">VBATSEL</span>: <span data-conditional="_adc_vref_,RM0440">VBAT</span> selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to control <span data-conditional="_adc_vref_,RM0440">VBAT</span>.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: V<sub>BAT</sub> channel disabled.<br/>1: V<sub>BAT</sub> channel enabled</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 23</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span data-conditional="_adc_vref_,RM0440" style="font-weight:Bold;">VSENSESEL</span>: <span data-conditional="_adc_vref_,RM0440">V</span><sub data-conditional="_adc_vref_,RM0440">TS</sub> selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to control <span data-conditional="_adc_vref_,RM0440">V</span><sub data-conditional="_adc_vref_,RM0440">TS</sub>.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Temperature sensor channel disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Temperature sensor channel enabled</p></td></tr><tr height="70.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 22</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">VREFEN</span>: V<sub>REFINT</sub> enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to enable/disable the V<sub>REFINT</sub> channel.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: V<sub>REFINT</sub> channel disabled<br/>1: V<sub>REFINT</sub> channel enabled</p></td></tr><tr height="293.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 21:18</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PRESC[3:0]</span>: ADC prescaler</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are set and cleared by software to select the frequency of the clock to the ADC. The clock is common for all the ADCs.</p><p class="TableIndent">0000: input ADC clock not divided<br/>0001: input ADC clock divided by 2<br/>0010: input ADC clock divided by 4<br/>0011: input ADC clock divided by 6<br/>0100: input ADC clock divided by 8<br/>0101: input ADC clock divided by 10<br/>0110: input ADC clock divided by 12<br/>0111: input ADC clock divided by 16<br/>1000: input ADC clock divided by 32<br/>1001: input ADC clock divided by 64<br/>1010: input ADC clock divided by 128<br/>1011: input ADC clock divided by 256<br/>other: reserved</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when the ADC is disabled (ADCAL = 0, JADSTART = 0, ADSTART = 0, ADSTP = 0, ADDIS = 0 and ADEN = 0). The ADC prescaler value is applied only when CKMODE[1:0] = 00.</p></td></tr><tr height="241.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 17:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CKMODE[1:0]: </span>ADC clock mode</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are set and cleared by software to define the ADC clock scheme (which is common to both master and slave ADCs):</p><p class="TableIndent">00: <span data-conditional="_adc_new_naming,_adc_vref_">adc_ker_ck</span> (x = 123) (Asynchronous clock mode), generated at product level (refer to <span class="CrossRef" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 6: Reset and clock control (RCC)</span>)</p><p class="TableIndent">01: <span data-conditional="_adc_new_naming,_adc_vref_">adc_hclk</span>/1 (Synchronous clock mode). This configuration must be enabled only if the AHB clock prescaler is set (HPRE[3:0] = 0xxx in RCC_CFGR register) and if the system clock has a 50% duty cycle.</p><p class="TableIndent">10: <span data-conditional="_adc_new_naming,_adc_vref_">adc_hclk</span>/2 (Synchronous clock mode)</p><p class="TableIndent">11: <span data-conditional="_adc_new_naming,_adc_vref_">adc_hclk</span>/4 (Synchronous clock mode)</p><p class="TableIndent"><br/></p><p class="TableIndent">In all synchronous clock modes, there is no jitter in the delay from a timer trigger to the start of a conversion.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when the ADCs are disabled (ADCAL = 0, JADSTART = 0, ADSTART = 0, ADSTP = 0, ADDIS = 0 and ADEN = 0).</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_" height="146.67px"><td data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:14</p></td><td data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_"><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MDMA[1:0]</span><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">:</span> Direct memory access mode for dual ADC mode </p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield is set and cleared by software. Refer to the DMA controller section for more details.</p><p class="TableIndent">00: MDMA mode disabled<br/>01: <span data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_,_noadc_dfsdm">Reserved</span><br/>10: MDMA mode enabled for 12 and 10-bit resolution<br/>11: MDMA mode enabled for 8 and 6-bit resolution</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no regular conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_adc_1adc,_adc_vref_" height="22.67px" style="display: none"><td data-conditional="_adc_1adc,_adc_vref_" style="display: none"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:0</p></td><td data-conditional="_adc_1adc,_adc_vref_" style="display: none"><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_" height="134.72px"><td data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 13</p></td><td data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_"><p class="Body" style="margin-top : 0.00pt;font-size : 9.00pt;"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DMACFG</span>: DMA configuration (for dual ADC mode)</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to select between two DMA modes of operation and is effective only when DMAEN = 1.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: DMA One Shot mode selected</p><p class="TableIndent">1: DMA Circular mode selected</p><p class="TableIndent">For more details, refer to <a href="#XREF_53109__1_6_5_Using_the_DMA10" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section : Managing conversions using the DMA</a></p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no regular conversion is ongoing).</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_" height="22.67px"><td data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 12</p></td><td data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_"><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_" height="86.67px"><td data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 11:8</p></td><td data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_"><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DELAY</span><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">:</span> Delay between 2 sampling phases </p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are set and cleared by software. These bits are used in dual interleaved modes. Refer to <a href="#XREF_54121__Table_49_10" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Table 179</a> for the value of ADC resolution versus DELAY bits values. </p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when the ADCs are disabled (ADCAL = 0, JADSTART = 0, ADSTART = 0, ADSTP = 0, ADDIS = 0 and ADEN = 0).</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_" height="22.67px"><td data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:5</p></td><td data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_"><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_" height="288.00px"><td data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 4:0</p></td><td data-conditional="_adc_2adc,_adc_3adc,_adc_5adc,_adc_vref_"><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DUAL[4:0]</span><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">:</span> Dual ADC mode selection </p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are written by software to select the operating mode.</p><p class="TableIndent">All the ADCs independent:</p><p class="TableIndent">00000: Independent mode</p><p class="TableIndent"><br/></p><p class="TableIndent">00001 to 01001: Dual mode, master and slave ADCs working together<br/>00001: Combined regular simultaneous + injected simultaneous mode<br/>00010: Combined regular simultaneous + alternate trigger mode<br/>00011: Combined Interleaved mode + injected simultaneous mode</p><p class="TableIndent">00100: Reserved<br/>00101: Injected simultaneous mode only<br/>00110: Regular simultaneous mode only<br/>00111: Interleaved mode only<br/>01001: Alternate trigger mode only</p><p class="TableIndent">All other combinations are reserved and must not be programmed</p><p class="TableBodyL"><br/></p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The software is allowed to write these bits only when the ADCs are disabled (ADCAL = 0, JADSTART = 0, ADSTART = 0, ADSTP = 0, ADDIS = 0 and ADEN = 0).</p></td></tr></table></div>

### 21.8.3 ADCx common regular data register for dual mode (ADCx\_CDR)    (x = 12 or 345)

Address offset: 0x30C

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

One interface controls ADC1 and ADC2, while the other interface controls ADC3, ADC4 and ADC5.
